solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It shows up some yobs, actually

indicators.note: shows up says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that something genuinely exposes a few of the local louts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' marks a run of letters hidden in 'yobs, actually'; in a down clue 'shows up' turns them so they read upwards. An ASBO was a British anti-social behaviour order, the court order typically handed to yobs (louts).
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun stands in for the thing the rest of the clue describes, the court order given to troublemakers.

clue.text: National leader offering three letters in a row?

definitions.meaning: read as '...', it names three consecutive letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A head of state who seems to be offering a trio of something lined up.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the name into G AND HI: G, H and I sit next to each other in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohandas Gandhi was the leader of the Indian independence movement, father of the nation.

clue.text: Ready and able to accommodate sport? That's nourishing food for you

parts.note: ready (readies) is slang for money, as is bread

indicators.note: to accommodate means to take in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: fit means able, capable
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A sporty, fit person praises a hearty meal as good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like an adjective meaning prepared, but 'the readies' is British slang for cash; 'to accommodate' signals one word taken inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The starchy fruit of a tropical tree is a staple, filling food when cooked.

clue.text: Head of big English college upheld English writer

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
in a down clue, upheld means held upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: COLL is an abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: The principal of a large English college lent support to an English author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheld' turns COLL so it reads upwards, giving LLOC.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilaire Belloc was an Anglo-French poet and essayist, known for his cautionary tales for children.

clue.text: Gas, including oxygen, beginning to materialise? It's not important

indicators.note: including means holding something inside

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly, to natter
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a gas with oxygen in it is starting to take solid form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' looks like a chemistry noun but is the verb to chat; 'including' puts O and M inside NATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dismissive idiom used to wave something away as unimportant.

clue.text: Love will have one in fix

indicators.note: will have means will contain, so one word holds the other

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, nil
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: Romance is going to land someone in a bit of a predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fix' looks like a noun for a predicament, but the definition is the verb to fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail something is to fasten it firmly in place, to fix it.

clue.text: Underwear? Grand passion raised when in particular brand

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a line is a particular brand of goods in a range
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means lifted upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: Intimate garments stir great passion when sold under a certain label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' makes the passion read upwards in this down clue, and 'in' sets the G-led result between the brand's third and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underclothing, especially delicate or decorative items.

clue.text: Period of study sees fishes being given name

parts.note: a school is a group of fishes swimming together
a term is a name or word for something

explanation.surface: A spell of study in which a shoal of fish gets christened.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the parts the teaching year divides into is a stretch of time spent studying.

clue.text: High-flier restraining ego in part of flight

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a star is a high-flier, a big success
I is the self, the ego

explanation.surface: A successful achiever keeps their vanity in check during part of an air journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests air travel, but it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is made up of individual steps, each one a single part.

clue.text: I manage leading pair of companies badly, but I can't imagine anyone else in the job!

definitions.text: I can't imagine anyone else in the job!

indicators.note: badly says these letters are put into a disordered new arrangement

parts.note: these letters are taken as written

indicators.note: the leading pair of a word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A boss who runs two firms poorly still insists nobody else could do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' shuffles IMANAGE plus CO, the first two letters of 'companies'.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is the kind of thing said by someone obsessed with self-importance.

clue.text: A third testicle? That's unusual

definitions.meaning: read literally, a spare testicle is an extra, odd one
as an adjective the word means eccentric or strange

explanation.surface: A medical oddity is described, then dismissed as merely unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Applied to a person or thing, the word means eccentric or strange.

clue.text: A line that gets cricket side run out quickly

parts.note: leg is the leg side of a cricket field, the side of the batter's legs
RO is the scorecard abbreviation for run out in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator's line about a team's batter being dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket field is divided into the off side and the leg side; a batter is run out when the stumps are broken before they reach the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical tempo marking tells players to perform at a brisk, lively pace.

clue.text: Long-established pop star rocks at the seaside

definitions.meaning: ... Richard has been a British pop singer since the 1950s
a steep rock face on a coast

explanation.surface: A veteran pop singer gives a rocking performance on the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard is a British singer with hits in every decade from the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: A high steep rock face, often found along a coastline above the sea.

clue.text: Stop after 24 hours?

parts.note: the idiom for knocking off work, read literally as ending once a full day has passed

explanation.surface: A question whether to halt once a full day has gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop working for the time being, read here as ending after one day.

clue.text: Guy getting doctor brought in to cure bishop's seat?

parts.note: cat is slang for a guy, a fellow

indicators.note: brought in to means put inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to heal is to cure

explanation.surface: A man calls in a doctor to treat a churchman's bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' reads like a chair, and the question mark flags the formal sense; 'brought in to' sets the doctor inside the cure, giving HEDRAL. 'Cat' for a man is jazz-era slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The church containing a bishop's throne, the cathedra, is the seat of a diocese.

clue.text: Reapplication of heat and I relax in delight

indicators.note: reapplication means laying the letters out again in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Applying warmth again helps someone unwind with pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhilarate someone is to thrill or elate them, filling them with joy.

clue.text: Member with strong impulse: see her getting upset about cold dairy product

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body
an urge is a strong impulse

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round another
getting upset means being knocked over and disordered, rearranging the letters

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A club member with a strong impulse to visit a woman finds her upset by a chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' rearranges SEEHER to RHEESE; 'about' wraps that round C, giving RCHEESE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent soft cheese originally from Limburg, a Belgian region, is a dairy food.

clue.text: Stay put when exam result comes out

definitions.meaning: to march on the spot, or wait without progressing
read literally, the time a grade is given

explanation.surface: Advice to wait patiently until the grades are published.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to march on the spot, hence to wait without making progress.

clue.text: Catch up with soldiers reaching one African city

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: to bag is to catch
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops meeting up in a city somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns BAG to GAB. OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaborone is the capital city of Botswana in southern Africa.

clue.text: Easily annoyed, showing a lot of anger, anger about bill

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most of it, losing its last letter

parts.note: ire is anger

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: to rile is to anger
a tab is a bill, as in a bar

explanation.surface: A tetchy diner shows plenty of rage over the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anger' appears twice, as noun then verb, so each supplies a different word; 'a lot of' drops the final letter and 'about' wraps the bill, giving RITABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Irritable describes someone quick to lose patience or take offence.

clue.text: Provide relief for current speaker, after upsetting manager

indicators.note: after upsetting means once turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: the current speaker refers to themselves as me
a boss is a manager

explanation.surface: Someone helps out the speaker who has just upset their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief' suggests help, but it is a raised design; 'current' is not electricity but 'present'.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to raise a design on a surface, producing a pattern in relief.

clue.text: Deputy Officer in Charge interrupting Mass, though having no power

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so it goes inside another word
having no power means losing P, the symbol for power

parts.note: a lump is a mass
OC is the abbreviation for Officer in Charge (or Commanding)

explanation.surface: A deputy officer breaks into a church service despite lacking authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service but is a lump; 'having no power' removes P to give LUM, and 'interrupting' puts OC inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A locum is a doctor or cleric standing in temporarily for another, a stand-in.

clue.text: Tax applied to revolutionary bow tie replacement

indicators.note: applied to means attached after, so this piece follows
revolutionary means turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an arc is a bow, a curve
VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A tax on a radical's bow tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow tie' wants to be one item; 'bow' is the arc and 'tie replacement' the definition. VAT is the UK's sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is neckwear worn in place of a necktie.

clue.text: Soldier with exposed emotions, one turning this?

definitions.text: Soldier with exposed emotions, one turning this?

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant

indicators.note: turning means facing about, so the words read backwards

parts.note: raw means emotionally exposed, as in raw feelings
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A soldier, emotionally laid bare, turns against war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' suggests an infantryman but here is the insect caste; 'turning' gives IWAR. The whole clue also pictures a traumatised fighter who rejects war.
explanation.definitionFit: A traumatised fighter turning pacifist becomes opposed to armed conflict.

clue.text: Ineffective operator heads for wall in monetary panic

indicators.note: heads means the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: A useless trader runs for the wall in a financial panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a weak, feeble person who gets nothing done.

clue.text: Brainy cooks adopting international dish

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so one piece goes inside
to cook is to doctor or rearrange, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Clever chefs take up a dish from around the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooks' looks like a noun for chefs but is the anagram signal for BRAINY.
explanation.definitionFit: Biryani is a South Asian rice dish cooked with spiced meat or vegetables.

clue.text: Vain Sarkozy's key when bringing in Germany

indicators.note: bringing in means taking inside, so one piece goes in

parts.note: Sarkozy, a former French president, would call a key (island) an ile
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A French president's conceited key to a deal involving Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: A key (cay) is a low island; French for island is ÎLE, signalled by the French president Sarkozy.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means vain or futile, as in idle threats or idle hopes.

clue.text: A marine, leading old servicewomen, capturing soldiers and weaponry

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so these pieces come first

parts.note: RM is the Royal Marines

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside

parts.note: the ATS was the Auxiliary Territorial Service, Britain's wartime women's army
men are soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: A marine at the head of a band of old servicewomen seizes troops and guns.
explanation.walkthrough: The ATS, the Auxiliary Territorial Service, was the British women's army branch in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Armaments are military weapons and equipment collectively.

clue.text: Track transport system that's behind time

indicators.note: behind means following, so this piece comes after

parts.note: rail is a transport system

explanation.surface: A railway network that is always running late.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path or route, or as a verb to follow a scent.
